title: Single affine cover criterion for local surjectivity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal B_S$ be its affine pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Let $F,G$ be sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on $\mathcal B_S$, and let $\phi:F\to G$ be a morphism. Then $\phi$ is locally surjective if and only if, for every object $U$ and section $y\in G(U)$, there exist an arrow $q:W\to U$ in $\mathcal B_S$ whose underlying scheme map is surjective and a section $x\in F(W)$ such that $\phi_W(x)=G(q)(y)$. Here locally surjective means that, for every $U,y$, the sieve of arrows along which $y$ lifts is covering.

source.place: isLocallySurjective_iff_of_isSheaf, lines 62-84; finite disjoint union of local lifting covers

proof.text: For local surjectivity, take the covering image sieve of y. Refine it by a finite jointly surjective affine-basis family and choose each local lift. The source-library sigmaCover is their finite disjoint union; exists_sigmaCover_glue glues the chosen sections with no overlap constraints. surjective_sigmaCoverπ supplies the single surjective arrow, and sigmaCover_ext with naturality proves its section has the required image. This is exactly the existing Lean proof. Empty schemes and empty finite families are included.

Conversely, the sieve of local lifts contains the singleton q. A surjective affine-basis arrow is a covering by generate_singleton_mem_topology; upward closure makes the image sieve covering. This is the reverse direction of the same existing Lean proof.

lean.statement:
lemma isLocallySurjective_iff_of_isSheaf {F G : S.AffineProEtᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (topology S) F) (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (topology S) G) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (topology S) φ ↔
      ∀ (X : S.AffineProEt) (y : G.obj (op X)), ∃ (W : S.AffineProEt) (q : W ⟶ X)
        (_ : Surjective q.left) (x : F.obj (op W)), φ.app (op W) x = G.map q.op y
